# Gower

![The sunset over Rhosili Bay on the Gower Peninsula, Wales. The beach can be seen in the distance and in the foreground three visitors walk along the cliff edge.](https://nt.global.ssl.fastly.net/binaries/content/gallery/website/national/regions/wales/places/rhosili-and-south-gower-coast/library/rhosili-bay-gower-peninsula-wales-1463934.jpg?auto=webp&width=767&crop=16:9&dpr=2%202x)Rhosili Bay on the Gower Peninsula \| © National Trust Images/Chris Lacey

Explore the UK's first designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The Gower Peninsula in South Wales has a beautifully diverse landscape with golden beaches, salt marsh and countryside teeming with wildlife.

## Things to see and do in Gower

![A young visitor in an orange t-shirt flying a kite on the beach at Rhosili and South Gower Coast](https://nt.global.ssl.fastly.net/binaries/content/gallery/website/national/regions/wales/places/rhosili-and-south-gower-coast/library/summer/flying-a-kite-rhosili-south-gower-wales-1504871.jpg?auto=webp&width=676&crop=16:9&dpr=2%202x)Flying a kite on the beach at Rhosili and South Gower Coast \| © National Trust Images/Chris Lacey

Coasts and beaches in GowerLearn more about what to see and do on a visit to Gower in South Wales, from swimming and sandcastle building in Rhosili Bay to hiking around Penmaen Burrows and Nicholaston. [Explore coasts and beaches in Gower](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/coast-beaches/coasts-and-beaches-in-gower)

Visiting Rhosili and South GowerA scenic spot for coastal walks, water sports and wildlife. With 3 miles of sandy beach there’s plenty of space for the whole family to play in the sand or fly a kite. [Plan your visit to Rhosili and South Gower](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/rhosili-and-south-gower-coast)

Cwm Ivy on the North Gower coastThere are two bird hides – Cheriton hide and Monterey hide, located either side of Cwm Ivy salt marsh, which also forms part of the wider Whiteford National Nature Reserve. [Plan your visit to Cwm Ivy](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/whiteford-and-north-gower)

## Our work in Gower

![Group of young adults walking through a sunflower field in summer, with sea in the background](https://nt.global.ssl.fastly.net/binaries/content/gallery/website/national/regions/wales/places/rhosili-and-south-gower-coast/library/visitors-sunflowers-rhosili-south-gower-coast-wales-1505109.jpg?auto=webp&width=676&crop=16:9&dpr=2%202x)Visitors enjoying the spectacular display of sunflowers at Rhosili, South Gower \| © National Trust Images/Chris Lacey

Our work at RhosiliRhosili has thrived in recent years thanks to our wildlife-friendly farming practices. By planting traditional arable crops and wildflower meadows, we have helped improve biodiversity and provide food sources for bees, butterflies and flocks of overwintering birds. [Learn more about our work in Gower](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/rhosili-and-south-gower-coast/our-work-at-rhosili)

Our work at Cwm IvyCwm Ivy marsh on the North Gower coast, is a salt marsh teeming with wildlife. It supports a thriving ecosystem from tiny, rare snails to grass snakes, otters, and bats. Learn more about our work at this special habitat near Whiteford sand dunes. [Learn more about Cwm Ivy](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/whiteford-and-north-gower/our-work-at-cwm-ivy)

## Places to stay in Gower

![Exterior of Rhossili Old Rectory, South Wales](https://nt.global.ssl.fastly.net/binaries/content/gallery/website/holidays/library/wales/rhossili-old-rectory/theoldrectory-exterior-mikehentonfeb201819.jpg?auto=webp&width=676&crop=16:9&dpr=2%202x)The old rectory in Rhosili \| © National Trust Images/Mike Henton

Holiday cottages in South WalesFrom coastal cottages with stunning sea views to secluded woodland locations there’s a holiday cottage for everyone on Gower. [Find a holiday cottage in South Wales](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/holidays/wales/cottages/south-wales)

![View of Powis Castle, perched above its terraced gardens, Powys, Wales, in autumn.](https://nt.global.ssl.fastly.net/binaries/content/gallery/website/national/regions/wales/places/powis-castle-and-garden/library/autumn/powis-castle-and-garden-autumn-powys-wales-1294060-1.jpg?auto=webp&width=767&crop=16:9&dpr=2%202x)

# Exploring the Gower Peninsula

Gŵyr (Gower), the first place in Britain to be named a National Landscape, features cliffs, woodlands and sparkling beaches. Adored by walkers, birdwatchers, sunbathers and surfers, here are 10 things not to miss on this 70-square-mile (180sq km) paradise.

SaveShare

## Exploring Worm’s Head

The most iconic sight on Gŵyr is this rocky promontory that snakes out into Bae Rhosili (Rhossili Bay): the name ‘worm’ comes from the Viking for ‘sea serpent’. The walk out to [Pen Pyrod](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/rhossili-and-south-gower-coast/trails/rhossili-headland-walk) (Worm's Head) is a fabulous adventure on a sunny day, but do check the tides, which are displayed on a board near the causeway – it’s only reachable for two hours either side of low tide. Even locals get it wrong: as a boy, the poet [Dylan Thomas](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4064) was marooned until midnight.

![Rhossili & Worm's Head 'Helvetia' wreck beneath the sunset at Gower Peninsula.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/S102-129-SP.jpg.webp?itok=HMyZ7AJX)

Pen Pyrod and the 'Helvetia' wreck, Gŵyr, West Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Gower’s best beaches

[Rhosili](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843187) regularly makes lists of the world’s best beaches, for very good reason: its three-mile (4.8km) golden sands feature towering cliffs and Pen Pyrod at one end, dunes at the other, and a genuine shipwreck in between. In summer, you can watch paragliders ridge-soaring the updrafts on Rhos Rhosili (Rhosili Downs).

This spectacular beach has long been a star of the small screen, featuring in a number of high-profile TV productions including BBC drama series such as _Doctor Who_ and _The Guest_. You can explore more about [Doctor Who filming locations in Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3006/) and discover other [TV and film locations across Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3132/).

![Sweeping sandy beach with a rectory positioned looking at the sea front](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2025-09/778245-wvw-h80-2526-rhossili-old-rectory-0034-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=RBSAAj-7)

![Side of a white painted house looking out to the sea ](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2025-09/778251-wvw-h80-2526-rhossili-old-rectory-0028-web-optimised-1920px.jpg.webp?itok=Oy3Q4vuJ)

Bae Rhosili, Gŵyr, West Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

Rhosili is also a brilliant spot for dogs, with wide open sands, plenty of room for four‑legged explorers to roam, whatever the season.

**Read more:** [Dog-friendly break in Gower with Lolly The Whippet](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6336)

For sheer natural beauty, [Bae y Tri Chlogwyn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1936407) (Three Cliffs Bay) is just as good: the Pennard Pill river cuts a deep cleft into the wooded hillside before emptying into a gorgeous bay, overlooked by the ruins of Pennard Castle and the eponymous three jagged cliffs. Strong currents mean that it isn’t ideal for swimming, and it’s a bit of a walk to reach it – but that makes it quieter, and even more special.

![Rhossili Bay](https://walesdmsmedia.newmindmedia.com/wsimgs/581027135D239A04173F5E14AD5CC5E8A2C1BFA1.jpg)

## Family‑friendly beaches near Mumbles

The first two beaches you hit on the way out of [Mwmbwls](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6186) (Mumbles) onto Gŵyr are also the easiest with small children.

[Bae Cas-wellt](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/caswell-bay-beach/) (Caswell Bay) and [Langland](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443779) have all the trimmings you need – parking, ice cream, toilets, shops – as well as Blue Flag Awards. The clifftop walk between the beaches is also a good introduction to coastal walking.

Is this one of the most picturesque sections of the [@walescoastpath](https://www.instagram.com/walescoastpath/?utm_source=ig_embed)? 😍

The 2 mile walk between Langland and Caswell Bay on the Gower Peninsula is known for its dramatic coastal scenery, with panoramic views stretching across the Bristol Channel. 🌊

The path is largely accessible with various viewpoints along the way. Facilities can be found at both ends of the route. 🏖️

## Hidden beaches on Gower

Pretty [Bae Pobbles](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/pobbles-bay-beach/) (Pobbles Bay) is tucked behind the iconic Three Cliffs at the end of a long-ish walk over cliffs and dunes, so it’s often overlooked. The same goes for [Traeth Bae Mewslade](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/mewslade-bay-beach/) (Mewslade Bay), which is overshadowed by neighbouring Pen Pyrod and Rhosili. But the least visited of all is Blue Pool Bay, accessible only after a yomp over dunes from [Traeth Bae Broughton](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/broughton-bay-beach/) (Broughton Bay) on the remote northwest corner.

## Top surf spots on the Gower Peninsula

Gŵyr has been a surfing hotspot for decades. When surfing here you can expect company from world class professionals like Patrick Langdon-Dark and Alys Barton, among others. The favourite break of two-time European professional surfing champion, Chris 'Guts' Griffiths is at [Langland](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443779), while [Llangennith](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/llangennith-beach/), on the northwest tip, is considered to be one of the [best surf spots in Wales for seasoned surfers](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3052) due to its reliable waves. For newbies wanting to give it a go, [Rhosili](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843187) and [Bae Caswell](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/caswell-bay-beach/) (Caswell Bay) are usually more suitable [surf spots for beginners](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3575) and there are several [operators offering surf lessons](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=surf&location=&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&subfilter%5B0%5D=Surfing&sector%5B0%5D=Activity&region%5B0%5D=West%20Wales&town%5B0%5D=Swansea) along the coast to help you learn to surf safely.

## Outdoor adventures on Gower

Gŵyr is deservedly known for its beaches so in addition to surfing there are plenty of other coastal activities on offer, such as coasteering and standup paddleboarding, but there are also adventures to be had on dry land. You can horse ride on the beaches or up on the moorland, or if you've a head for heights, rock-climb and abseil on the sea cliffs. Mountain bikers can find miles of rough track along [Rhos Rhosili](https://www.swansea.gov.uk/rhossili) and [Cefn Bryn](https://www.swansea.gov.uk/cefnbryn) common, while road cyclists will love the quiet lanes on the north side of the peninsula.

Use our [search function to find a full list of activity providers](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=Gower&location=&lat=51.5966706&long=-4.1698781&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&sector%5B0%5D=Activity).

## Best walks on the Gower Peninsula

For a relatively compact area, there’s a huge variety of landscapes on Gŵyr. The [Wales Coast Path](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3208/) runs around the coastline, taking in the dramatic cliffs and coves of the south, and the quieter coastal salt marshes of the north. [The Gower Way](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/things-to-do/outdoors/walking-routes/the-gower-way/) cuts for 35 miles (56km) right through the middle. [Visit Swansea Bay](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/things-to-do/outdoors/walking-routes/) and the [National Trust](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/rhossili-and-south-gower-coast/lists/top-walks-on-gower) have come up with lists of their own favourite walks of varying lengths. Get more inspiration from our guide to [walks near Abertawe](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6451). Our own personal favourite is anything with a pub at the end. Talking of which…

## Pubs and places to drink on Gower

A lot of walks/cycles in the uplands tend to gravitate towards [The King Arthur](https://www.kingarthurhotel.co.uk/) in Reynoldston, a proper roaring-log-fire country pub beneath Cefn Bryn, the highest point on Gŵyr. Another good local is the award-winning [Britannia Inn](https://www.britanniagower.com/) at Llanmadoc, whose beer garden has lovely views down to the Burry Inlet. And basically, anywhere that sells a pint of [The Gower Brewery](https://gowerbrewery.com/)'s Gower Gold.

## Where to eat on the Gower Peninsula

The [Beach House](https://beachhouseoxwich.co.uk/) won AA Restaurant of the Year in Wales within a year of opening in a fantastic beachfront spot in Oxwich Bay. Chef Hywel Griffith is a master of seasonal, local ingredients: the fish is landed by boats that bob in the sea just beyond the terrace, veg from local farms, and [lamb](https://www.gowersaltmarshlamb.co.uk/) from the salt marshes a few miles away. It also holds a Michelin Star. While you're there, take time to relax in [Tŷ Sawna](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/569531), in one of two barrel saunas with wood-fired stoves and stunning ocean views.

Gŵyr is also the spiritual home of those twin Welsh delicacies, cockles and laverbread. The laver (seaweed) is harvested from the shoreline, while cockles came (and still do) from the sandy estuary at Penclawdd on the north coast. If you see either/both on the menu anywhere on Gŵyr, go for it.

## Gower’s rich history and heritage

The oldest buried human remains in Britain were found on Gŵyr, dating back more than 30,000 years: the ['Red Lady'](https://oumnh.ox.ac.uk/red-lady-of-paviland-0) of Paviland (who later turned out to be a fella). The uplands are littered with Neolithic remains, most notably the burial chamber topped by the 25-ton [Arthur's Stone](https://historypoints.org/index.php?page=arthurs-stone-or-maen-ceti-gower). The Normans tried to oust the Welsh from Gŵyr in the 11th and 12th centuries by bringing in Flemish settlers, and there’s still a noticeable difference in place-names, accent and dialect between the Welsh north and Anglicised south of the peninsula.

Follow the [Legendary Castles Trail](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/inspirations/swansea-bay-trails/legendary-castles-trail/) to visit coastal castles including [Castell Weble](https://www.visitwales.com/product/516106), [Castell Oxwich](https://cadw.gov.wales/visit/places-to-visit/castell-oxwich) and Pennard Castle. [The Gower Heritage Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/517711) is a good place to learn about rural culture, while the [Gower Festival](https://www.gowerfestival.org/) brings high-calibre classical performers to a dozen ancient local churches each July. There’s also a strong folk tradition on Gŵyr, best experienced at the annual [Gower Folk Festival](http://www.gowerfolkfestival.co.uk/) in June.

## FAQs about visiting the Gower Peninsula

- ### What are the best things to do on the Gower Peninsula?











Penrhyn Gŵyr (the Gower Peninsula) is famous for its award-winning [beaches](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#beaches), spectacular [coastal walks](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#walking), [outdoor adventures](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#outdoor), excellent [dining](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#dining) and [heritage](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#history) sites. Popular activities include exploring [Rhosili Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843187) and [Bae y Tri Chlogwyn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1936407) (Three Cliffs Bay), walking the [Gower Coast Path](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/things-to-do/outdoors/walking-routes/gower-coast-path/), visiting [Pen Pyrod](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#WormsHead) (Worm's Head) and enjoying watersports such as [surfing](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#surfing) and paddleboarding.

- ### Which is the best beach on the Gower Peninsula?











[Rhosili Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843187) is often regarded as the best beach on Penrhyn Gŵyr (the Gower Peninsula) thanks to its three miles of golden sand, dramatic cliffs and stunning views. Other visitor favourites include [Bae y Tri Chlogwyn](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1936407) (Three Cliffs Bay), [Oxwich Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/553031) and [Bae Cas-wellt](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/caswell-bay-beach/) (Caswell Bay).

- ### Is the Gower Peninsula good for families?











Yes, Penrhyn Gŵyr (the Gower Peninsula) is a fantastic family destination, offering safe sandy [beaches](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#family), rock pooling, wildlife spotting and family-friendly walks. Beaches such as [Y Mwmbwls](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6186) (Mumbles), [Bae Cas-wellt](https://www.visitswanseabay.com/listings/caswell-bay-beach/) (Caswell Bay), [Langland](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1443779) and [Oxwich Bay](https://www.visitwales.com/twg-product/553031) provide facilities including cafés, parking and toilets.

- ### Can you walk to Worm's Head?











Yes, visitors can walk to [Pen Pyrod](https://www.visitwales.com/destinations/west-wales/swansea-bay/exploring-gower-peninsula#WormsHead) (Worm's Head) from Rhossili, but only during safe periods around low tide. It's important to check tide times before setting out, as the causeway becomes inaccessible when the tide comes in.
